claims.text: The starting material is homogenized Al0.7CoCrFeNi.
The starting alloy has a dual-phase FCC/B2 lamellar structure.
The starting alloy exhibits strong-yet-brittle behavior.
Incoherent interfaces in the starting alloy promote dislocation pile-ups, local stress concentrations, and interfacial microcracking.
The proposed intervention is HPHT treatment in a hexahedron-anvil apparatus.
The proposed HPHT treatment uses 6 GPa, 1473 K, and a two-hour dwell followed by controlled cooling and decompression.
The specified HPHT treatment will transform the lamellar colonies into a hierarchically patterned microstructure.
The HPHT-generated hierarchical microstructure will contain coherent interfaces.
Coherent interfaces will facilitate preferential dislocation transfer from the softer FCC phase into the harder B2 phase.
Improved dislocation transfer will relieve local stress concentrations and reduce interfacial cracking.
The refined hierarchical pattern will activate dislocation motion, stacking faults, microbands, and twinning.
The multiple deformation mechanisms will make plastic deformation more uniform and suppress catastrophic cracking.
HPHT treatment will approximately double the alloy's tensile strength to about 1150 MPa.
HPHT treatment will increase tensile ductility to about 36%.
HPHT treatment will change fracture behavior from catastrophic interfacial cracking to distributed microcracking.
Conventional arc-melted and cast eutectic high-entropy alloys have limited room-temperature ductility and brittleness caused by incoherent internal interfaces.
The benefits are expected only at the specified HPHT conditions that generate the coherent hierarchical microstructure.
Conventional hot isostatic pressing or thermomechanical treatment at similar temperatures but lower pressures will not produce the same enhancements.
Prior studies on similar alloy systems support the proposed transformation mechanism and simultaneous improvement in strength and ductility.
